reason: All key premises are directly supported by the cited evidence from PMC11606435, which reports that interstitial-driven LCO domains evolve and enlarge during cryogenic deformation, promote cross-slip and wavy slip, and lead to ultrahigh yield strength with satisfactory ductility. The hypothesis accurately represents these findings.
premises: Interstitial solutes in FCC HEAs promote incipient LCO formation.
Cryogenic, dynamic tensile loading enhances growth/coarsening of LCO domains.
Enlarged LCO domains promote dislocation cross-slip and a transition to wavy slip.
This mechanism simultaneously increases yield strength and work-hardening without compromising ductility.
